To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of DNA methyltransferase inhibitor SGI-110 (guadecitabine) and histone-deacetylase inhibitor MS275 (entinostat) synergistically reverses the epithelial mesenchyme transition in triple negative (TN) breast cancer by targeting multiple signaling pathways.
the combination of Sgi-110 with MS-275 synergistically inhibits the growth and stemness of TNBC by reversing EMT and inducing apoptosis.
DNMTi/HDACi exert antineoplastic effect in TNBC through reprogramming EMT.

the development of novel epigenetic therapies for TNBC.
the epigenetic reprogramming and reversal of the aggressive phenotype in TNBC.
the epigenetic mechanisms that underlie EMT and provides novel insights into the development of new therapies against EMT and TNBC.

the combination of Sgi-110 with MS-275 is a promising therapeutic approach in TNBC.
the combined treatment of SGI- 110 and MS275 exerts synergistic antitumor effects in TNBC cells, and that the combined treatment exerts antitumor effects through reversing EMT.
this study provides a new strategy to epigenetically treat TNBC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
epigenetic reprogramming is a promising therapeutic target for TNBC.
we developed an effective combination therapy for the treatment of aggressive breast cancer by targeting multiple signaling pathways and reversing the EMT process.
the combination of Sgi-110 and MS-275 is a promising treatment for triple negative breast cancer.

we identified two new agents that are highly effective in treating TNBC cells with EMT.
